not_applicable: end_state:pcr_plate (the source paper does not determine the exact volumes; composition checked instead)

items.evidence: Valid apiLevel 2.15 and P20 volumes of 1–5 µL are fine, but the protocol tells the user to manually transfer all 96 reactions from the Corning pcr_plate into a different PCR plate. That is needless extra handling that puts samples at risk.
add_reagent picks up a fresh tip and drops it for every transfer. The tip_before_aspirate, no_cross_contamination and tip_dropped_at_end checks all pass.

The protocol invents a manual transfer into a separate 0.2 mL PCR plate, a gel electrophoresis step, and assumed primer dilutions and cycling values. The paper's OT-2 workflow runs the reaction in the destination plate.
Each 10 µL well gets 5 µL 2x Q5 (1x final) first, then 4 µL primer pair, then 1 µL colony template last.
Primer and colony wells map to the same-named pcr_plate wells (primer_plate[destination.well_name], colony_plate[destination.well_name]) across all 96 wells, each used once.
The comments record sealing and a Q5 program: 98 °C for 30 s, then 30 cycles of 98 °C 10 s, 65 °C 20 s and 72 °C 30 s, then 72 °C for 2 min and a 4 °C hold.

judge.summary: The agent builds correct 10 µL reactions with the right order, fresh tips and a one-to-one well mapping, and it records a sensible Q5 program. It loses robot_practice and fidelity because it adds an invented manual transfer to a different PCR plate, plus a gel step and assumed primer concentrations.
